findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed that single-service and single-use articles and utensils were stored with the food-contact surfaces upright, including plastic cutlery single-use food cartons and nacho cheese holders. Customers and staff could potentially touch multiple food-contact surfaces when reaching for a utensil or a carton. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and utensils were flipped so that only there handles were upright, and cartons were flipped or placed underneath a closed shelf to protect the food-contact surfaces from debris from above. PIC and Inspector discussed additional ways that single-use utensils could be stored, including horizontal in either cleanable or disposable containers, as long as all the utensils are facing the same direction, so only handles will be touched when dispensed. Ensure that single-service and single-use utensils and articles are stored such that contamination of food-contact surfaces is prevented.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the individual trash receptacles in the stalls of the women’s bathroom do not have lids/covers. PIC was notified and Inspector discussed that covered trash receptacles are required in bathroom facilities used by women per IL Food Code, as it is more hygienic and protects plumbing from improperly flushed items. Inspector also discussed that upcoming Food Code updates (based on the 2026 FDA Food Code) will expand this need to all bathroom stalls, not just bathrooms used by women. Ensure all toilet rooms used by women have covered trash receptacles.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed multiple large pieces of equipment that are no longer in use because they are completely inoperable and not able to be repaired, included two 3-door coolers, 2 ovens, 1 hot box (requires a gas hookup which doesn’t exist), several mobile bar carts, and some coffee and tea pots. PIC was notified. Ensure that the premises is free of items that are unnecessary to the operation such as equipment that is nonfunctional or no longer used.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the table in the back of the kitchen (near the ice machine) holding various coffee/tea machines and the spray nozzle sink is not properly sealed to the wall. The caulking is deteriorating in quality and pulled away from the wall. Since the table is not easily removable from the wall the current caulking must be removed and the table re-caulked to the wall. Ensure that the table is sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employees fail to use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector discussed with the PIC and instructed them to educate employees about the proper hand washing procedure. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not present in the employee restrooms, the mezzanine concession stands, and the SW main floor concession stand. Handwashing signs were provided and placed in the concession stands by kitchen manager. Maintenance will be made aware of the need to post handwashing signs in employee restrooms. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.citation_text:
3-201.11 Bags of leftover cheese sauce that were previously heated and cooled were observed in the kitchen walk-in cooler. Current risk classification of Class II medium risk does not allow for cooling and reheating of hot TCS foods. Bags of cheese sauce were discarded, and new bags of cheese sauce were heated for use. **See HACCP Topic Section for additional information**
Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with the law

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold buildup was observed on the ceiling behind the baffle in the ice machine bin. Cleaning frequency was discussed. Ensure proper cleaning and sanitizing of the ice machine as needed per manufacturer directions. 
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed components such as ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sanitizer in spray bottles at concession stands had concentrations at 0ppm and less than 100ppm. Solutions were old and in need of changing. Fresh solution dispensed for the spray bottle to be used at the NW main concession stand for today’s event was observed at 200ppm. Ensure spray bottles of sanitizer are checked with test strips to verify concentration and refreshed as needed prior to concentration becoming weak and ineffective.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Chemical spray bottles pre-labeled as Purple Power cleaner contained old Quat solutions. A bottle of degreaser in the NW main concession stand was also not labeled. Proper labeling of chemicals was discussed, and spray bottles were properly labeled during inspection.
 Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.citation_text:
5-103.12 Cold water handle was stuck at the kitchen handwashing sink. Once turned to allow for cold water, there was very little pressure, and the water was discolored. The hot water, which was working prior to turning on the cold water, was then observed to also be discolored and lacking in pressure. Maintenance will be replacing the faucet and gaskets. 
Until the handwashing sink is repaired and functioning properly, the first basin at the kitchen 3 part sink will be used for handwashing. Dish soap was available at the sink, and paper towels were provided. Ensure basins are cleaned prior to setting up the sinks for ware washing at the end of food service. 
Hot and cold water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed hot dog to be 121F. Ensure foods hot held at 135F or above. Corrected. Hot Dogs will be used in 4 hours or less (from ~1545).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed ice machine to be soiled with yellow residue. Clean non-food contact surfaces as needed.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Sanitation bucket (spray bottle) did not contain proper sanitizer. Spray bottle was replaced with proper sanitizer (quat 200ppm). PIC stated all other stands will have proper sanitizer present during operation.
750-800b To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled: (1) the popcorn machine in the concession stand in the mezzanine and (2) the can opener blade in the basement kitchen. Clean and maintain food contact surfaces to prevent cross contamination. Management cleaned can opener blade during the inspection to correct the violation. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
(1) Observed nacho trays stored with the food contact surface exposed in the northwest main concession stand. Store single service items in a manner that protects the food contact surface (inverted). (2) Observed single service popcorn cups stored on the floor in the dry storage area in the kitchen. Single service items should be stored six inches off the floor.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floor in the walk in cooler to be soiled with beer. Clean and maintain floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 Basement hand sink was broken. Repair sink.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750.1210a Observed a leak in the ceiling of the dry storage area. Repair leak.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed gaps around the wall areas and prep table in upstairs concession stands. Seal the gaps (caulk).
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the bottom the coffee machine to have a buildup of debris near the water spout. Clean the bottom area.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed the single  service boats to be stored upright on the counter top. Invert the single service containers.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed gaps under the doors to the outside of the building. Repair the bottoms of the doors.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.
